primitives.verbatim_quote: - Best ρ: **-0.02** (weaker low-score correction than the textbook -0.05 — with team effects properly fit, τ's job shrinks).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\rho': 'dimensionless Dixon-Coles adjustment parameter', 'ξ': 'time-decay rate (days^{-1})', 'τ': 'temporal smoothing window'}
primitives.assumptions: Poisson scoring independence conditional on latent team strengths; team strength parameters absorb league mean; temporal decay captures aging information.
primitives.breakdown_regime: ξ → 0 (flat weighting) reverts to Dixon-Coles; ξ → ∞ (no decay) ignores temporal structure entirely.

layer2.mapping: The time-decay ξ maps directly onto the NFL covariate engine's exponential forgetting kernel exp(-λt). Both implement a continuous-time survival function that downweights older data. This establishes a rigorous link between match-level dependence models and dynamic team-value updating.
layer2.telemetry: Evaluate out-of-sample log-loss on held test sets (2024-25 EPL matches) against a flat-weight baseline. Additionally, monitor the stability of ρ estimates across rolling training windows to detect structural breaks.

primitives.name: Karlis-Ntzoufras full EM
primitives.verbatim_quote: - **Research finding: at league level the shared-component correlation vanishes** — once team strengths absorb the mean structure, soccer score covariance is ~0.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\lambda_3': 'KN shared-component precision parameter', 'σ^2': 'marginal variance of team strength latent variables', 'IG': 'inverse-gamma prior distribution'}
primitives.assumptions: Independent Poisson likelihood for each team's scoring intensity; hierarchical Gamma-Poisson mixture; EM algorithm maximizes the observed-data likelihood via alternating expectation and maximization steps.
primitives.breakdown_regime: λ_3 → ∞ recovers the independent Poisson model; λ_3 → 0 introduces perfect correlation.

layer2.mapping: The Karlis-Ntzoufras EM framework reduces to the independent Poisson assumption when λ_3 vanishes. This mirrors the NFL covariate engine's separation of league-mean adjustments from team-specific deviations. By absorbing the mean structure into the league-level parameters, the residual covariance becomes negligible, justifying the use of simpler, independent-process models for prediction.
layer2.telemetry: Compare the converged log-likelihoods of the full EM versus the independent limit. Check whether the estimated λ_3 posterior distribution collapses to near-zero values across multiple runs with different initializations.

primitives.name: Flex table correlation sensitivity
primitives.verbatim_quote: This is the market-as-prior doctrine **proven on hard data**: the product is the blend, never the naked m
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'P(all\\space 3)': 'Probability of winning all three legs in a 3-leg parlay', '\\rho': 'Equicorrelated copula parameter (pairwise correlation)', 'EV': 'Expected value for the player', 'hold': 'Operator hold percentage'}
primitives.assumptions: Equicorrelated multivariate Bernoulli outcomes with common pairwise correlation; independent Bernoulli trials at fair probability 0.5; parlay payout structure.
primitives.breakdown_regime: \rho → 0 (independence) yields the product of individual probabilities; \rho → 1 (perfect positive dependence) collapses the multi-leg bet to a single-leg equivalent.

layer2.mapping: The observed negative player expectation in Flex tables arises because bookmakers embed a 2% to 6% vig into each leg, pushing the effective win probability above 50%. The copula correlation parameter \rho quantifies how these embedded edges interact across legs. A high enough \rho can amplify the vig's impact through compounding, explaining why even seemingly attractive combinatorial bets become losing propositions in practice. This connects to the NFL engine's multi-period risk aggregation under serial dependence.
layer2.telemetry: Measure the realized hold rates on Flex parlays versus the theoretical hold implied by estimated ρ. Use transaction-level data to validate whether the copula model accurately predicts the degree of bettor clustering.
